# Overview

1- Leg size
2- Sex identified

```{r calling Rpackages}
library(here)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(glmmTMB)
library(DHARMa)
library(emmeans)
```

```{r importing the data}

# plan 1
data_leg <- read.table(here("data","raw","data_additional1.tsv"), header = T, stringsAsFactors = T, sep='\t')

# creating a long table of data_leg
leg_long <- data_leg %>%
  pivot_longer(cols=Leg.I:Leg.IV,
               names_to = "legid",
               values_to = "size")


# plan 2
data_sex <- read.table(here("data","raw","data_additional2.tsv"), header = T, stringsAsFactors = T, sep='\t')
data_sex[is.na(data_sex)] <- 0

# creating a long table of data_sex (honestly, I don't think this is helpful because the data does not identify which leg it was lost in terms of side)
sex_long <- data_sex %>%
  mutate(id = 1:nrow(data_sex)) %>%
  mutate(sex = factor(ifelse(data_sex$Male==1,"M","F"))) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols=Leg.I:Leg.IV,
               names_to = "legid",
               values_to = "autotomy")
sex_long <- sex_long[,-c(3,4)]

# creating an summarised data frame
sex_sum <- sex_long %>%
  group_by(sex, legid) %>%
  summarise (autotomy = sum(autotomy), .groups = "drop")
```


# ANOVA for testing if legs have different size

```{r}
boxplot(size ~ legid, leg_long)

m <- lm(size ~ legid, leg_long)
plot(m)
anova(m)

m_pos <- aov(size ~ legid, leg_long)
TukeyHSD(m_pos)
```

Leg II > Leg IV > Leg I = Leg III
